transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, yeah… I guess what brings me in is this constant restless feeling. It’s like I’ve got a little motor humming under my skin, especially anytime I’m expected to just sit still and listen. Like at staff meetings at work, or even church event briefings—places where you’re supposed to be respectful and just sit there—I’ll start shifting around in my chair, crossing and uncrossing my legs, leaning forward, leaning back, that kind of thing.

And if it goes on too long, I’ll end up standing up or finding some excuse to move—like getting water, checking something, saying I need to step out for a second. I don’t always mean to be disruptive, but sitting still feels almost uncomfortable, like my body is pushing me to get up even when my mind knows I should stay put. That’s the main thing I’m here about.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or needing to move even when you’re not in situations where you have to sit still, like when you’re at home relaxing or trying to focus on a task?

Yeah, I do. It’s not just when somebody tells me I have to sit still. Even on my own time, I don’t really settle. Like on my shifts, I’ll go from mopping one hallway to checking the trash in the break room to straightening chairs in a meeting room, and then I’ll notice something else and move right into that. It’s like I’m always looking for the next thing to do, even if nothing’s urgent.

And at home it’s kind of the same. After work, I’ll tell myself I’m going to sit down, but then I end up in the garage puttering around, re-sorting tools, moving things from one shelf to another, cleaning up a corner that didn’t really need it right then. I don’t always feel like I’m doing it on purpose, exactly. Sitting down just doesn’t come naturally unless I’m really worn out.
When did you first start noticing this restlessness and need to keep moving? Was this something you felt even as a child, like before you were a teenager?

Yeah, definitely before I was a teenager. I mean, thinking back, it was there in grade school pretty clearly. I can remember getting in trouble for popping up out of my seat when I wasn’t supposed to, like I’d forget I was supposed to stay sitting, or I’d just feel like I had to get up for some reason.

And I talked over the teacher a lot, too—not trying to be rude, exactly, but I’d jump in before she was done, or I’d rush ahead on an assignment before the directions were even finished. Then I’d have to be called back and told, “No, that’s not what we’re doing yet,” or “Wait until I’m done explaining.” That happened enough that I remember it, and I’m 56 now, so it must’ve made an impression.

My mother used to say I was “wound too tight” even as a kid. That was her phrase. Like I had this extra energy I couldn’t shut off. So, yeah, it’s not something that just started recently—it feels like it’s been part of me since I was little.
